run.note: Seeded demo fixture. Severity and likelihood are proposals. Nothing here is a confirmed hazard log entry until a Clinical Safety Officer signs it (DCB0160 3.3.2).

standard.legal_basis: Section 250, Health and Social Care Act 2012

entries.hazard_name: Severe allergy presented as severity Unknown in an active record at go-live
entries.hazard_description: Legacy allergy records whose severity cannot be parsed are migrated with severity Unknown and remain active and visible, while the clinical design assumes the panel is empty and severity is elicited from the patient at first appointment. Two approved designs, one panel.
causes: FLLD-DM-04 DM-04-R05 defaults unparseable severity to Unknown and keeps the record active
FLLD-DM-04 DM-04-R03 renders every migrated record visible at go-live
FLLD-CLIN-11 CLIN-11-R01/R05 assume an empty panel and patient-elicited severity
Regex derivation demonstrably misses anaphylaxis across a line break (dry-run extract)
entries.clinical_effect: A prescriber sees an active allergy with severity Unknown for a patient with a documented anaphylaxis. Emergency orders are exempt from the reconciliation hard-stop, so an emergency drug order can be placed against the Unknown record. The reconciliation appointment that the clinical design relies on is the encounter in progress.
existing_controls: CLIN-11-R04 ePMA hard-stop on non-emergency orders (does not cover emergency orders)
entries.severity_rationale: Death of a single patient from an anaphylactic reaction to a drug given against an Unknown severity record is a credible worst case.
entries.likelihood_rationale: 1.4 million records, regex derivation shown to fail on a real extract, and the failure mode produces an active record rather than an exception.
proposed_controls: Decide which design governs the panel at go-live and withdraw the other (CSG decision, minuted)
If legacy records are migrated, hold them in a quarantined, non-prescribing state rather than active with Unknown severity
Remove the emergency exemption or surface an explicit unverified-allergy banner on emergency orders
entries.proposed_owner_role: Clinical Safety Officer (Dr Fiona Gallagher) with Lead Migration Architect

evidence.excerpt: the record shall be migrated with severity defaulted to "Unknown" and shall remain active and visible
shall be unpopulated and empty at go-live for all migrated patients
never inferred or derived from automated algorithms or unverified historical free-text notes
Emergency orders are exempt from the hard-stop.
the record came through as severity Unknown

entries.hazard_name: Unmapped legacy allergen coded as No known allergy
entries.hazard_description: Any legacy allergen that fails SNOMED subset matching is assigned concept 716186003, No known allergy, with the original text demoted to a secondary note. The record asserts the absence of an allergy the patient has.
causes: FLLD-DM-04 DM-04-R02 fallback code for unmapped items
field-mapping.csv Row 4 implements the same fallback
FLLD-CLIN-11 CLIN-11-R02 prohibits legacy data populating a clinical field; the fallback is not treated as legacy data
entries.clinical_effect: Drug-allergy interaction alerts cannot fire on a No known allergy record. A prescriber is positively told the patient has no allergy.
existing_controls: Legacy text retained in secondary notes (not surfaced to the prescribing workflow)
entries.severity_rationale: The fallback applies to every unmatched record in a 1.4 million record migration; more than one patient could be affected.
entries.likelihood_rationale: Best-effort matching of free-text substance labels will leave a material residue unmatched; the rate is unmeasured.
proposed_controls: Replace the 716186003 fallback with an unresolved-allergen placeholder that blocks DAI and prompts reconciliation
Report the unmatched rate from the dry run before cutover
entries.proposed_owner_role: Clinical Safety Officer with Solution Assurance SME (Arthur Pendelton)

evidence.excerpt: Unmapped items shall be assigned SNOMED code 716186003 (No known allergy)
SNOMED CT NHS UK subset map; unmapped -> 716186003
Legacy allergy data must never populate a clinical field

entries.hazard_name: Approved design and build artefacts disagree on severity derivation; the decision exists only in chat
entries.hazard_description: Severity derivation was cancelled verbally and in the mapping sheet on 3 March. The approved FLLD-DM-04 v3.0 still mandates it. The walkthrough that would have minuted the decision was cancelled and no change request was raised.
causes: Decision taken in a Teams channel, not propagated to the approved artefact
Joint walkthrough cancelled; formal minuting skipped
No change request raised against FLLD-DM-04
entries.clinical_effect: Which behaviour ships is determined by which document the developer read. Either outcome is uncontrolled: derivation reintroduces HZ-001, suppression without a design change leaves Unknown defaults undefined.
entries.severity_rationale: Consequence is an uncontrolled build outcome feeding HZ-001; direct harm depends on which branch ships.
entries.likelihood_rationale: Dry run is scheduled against the current artefacts and the documentation update is explicitly deferred.
proposed_controls: Raise and approve a change request against FLLD-DM-04 before the dry run
Minute the 3 March decision in the Clinical Risk Management File (DCB0160 3.1.4)

evidence.excerpt: We can't derive severity from free text, it's a prescribing risk.
Do not migrate - free text derivation cancelled by Pharmacy SME
shall be algorithmically inferred from legacy free-text clinical notes
The approved PDF still states DM-04-R04 and DM-04-R05 are active.

entries.hazard_name: Ward location codes migrate through an undefined lookup
entries.hazard_description: Row 12 migrates WARD_LOCATION_CODE via a Ward Master reference that no approved design defines. The gap is acknowledged in the channel and parked.
causes: No design artefact for ward-level location translation
Mapping row left at Migrate=Y pending a response
entries.clinical_effect: Inpatient allergy records reject at load or attach to the wrong care setting; misattributed care setting can misdirect ward-level alerts.
existing_controls: DM-04-R09 staging exception queue, 72-hour manual resolution
entries.severity_rationale: Mis-located records are recoverable through the exception queue; harm requires a second failure.
entries.likelihood_rationale: Legacy ward codes without a translation are certain to exist; the volume is unknown.
proposed_controls: Set Row 12 to Migrate=N until a translation design is approved, or produce the design

evidence.excerpt: Direct lookup pending Ward Master ref
there is no approved design document for ward-level location translation

entries.hazard_name: Paediatric safeguarding note truncated by migration; ownership declined
entries.hazard_description: A safeguarding flag held only in free-text CLINICAL_COMMENTS sits beyond the 4000-character truncation in Row 10. The question of ownership was raised in the channel and redirected out of it. No decision is recorded anywhere.
causes: Safeguarding information held in uncoded free text in the legacy system
Ownership declined by the migration workstream and not picked up
entries.clinical_effect: A child's safeguarding flag is silently lost at cutover. The paediatric verification flag (DM-04-R08) covers allergy records only.
entries.severity_rationale: Loss of a safeguarding flag for a child is a credible route to severe harm.
entries.likelihood_rationale: Requires a note longer than 4000 characters with the flag at the end; at least one such record is known.
proposed_controls: Scan legacy CLINICAL_COMMENTS for safeguarding terms before truncation and route hits to a coded field or an exception
Assign an owner outside the migration workstream and record it
entries.proposed_owner_role: UNASSIGNED. Proposed: Trust Safeguarding Lead, via the Clinical Safety Officer

evidence.excerpt: If Row 10 truncates at 4000 characters the safeguarding note is at the end and will be cut. Who owns that?
Not us, that's a PAS safeguarding question.
